question:
Let O be the center of a circle and P be a point outside the circle. If PAB is a secant of the circle which cuts the circle at A and B and PT is the tangent drawn from P, then find the length of PT.

PA = 3 cm and AB = 9 cm.
solution:
Given:

Let O be the center of a circle and P be a point outside the circle. If PAB is a secant of the circle which cuts the circle at A and B and PT is the tangent drawn from P, then find the length of PT.

PA = 3 cm and AB = 9 cm.

Concept used:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a86fd2aad8b6c6b9ac9881d3effca66ee0553cfe9c40a859a64381f330b5eef8.png] 

If SUV and SW are a secant and a tangent respectively drawn from an external point S on a circle whose center is at C, then SU × SV = SW²

Calculation:

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/365e8f35ec334a36e53b268d8b1c196d424d13ecc393acfc77979c8e5e0352e7.png] 

​According to the concept,

PA × PB = PT²

⇒ 3 × (3 + 9) = PT²

⇒ PT² = 36

⇒ PT = √36

⇒ PT = 6

∴ The measure of PT is 6 cm.
